ledger.claim: The free waiting period in force for this trip is 300 seconds, not the 180-second default. trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec carries 300 for this STANDARD-zone trip, and the arrival derivation reads the same 300 seconds as the STANDARD minimum dwell. POL-NS-01(c) therefore requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of 300 seconds before any no-show fee can be charged against this rider, and POL-NS-06 measures the fee against that same figure.

The driver's own trace measures his in-geofence dwell at 210 seconds. It contains exactly one qualifying in-geofence interval, running from 07:45:10 to 07:48:40 - 22 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius - which is 90 seconds short of the 300 seconds the fee requires. On those numbers the cancellation fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-06 and is refunded in full; because the stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius, POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance or wrong block) has no purchase here and the only live question is dwell.

The dwell clock does not run from the arrival tap. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, which this trace places at 07:45:10 - 210 seconds after the arrived event the trip record carries at 07:41:40, and 240 seconds after the 07:41:10 the driver asserts in his own statement. The driver's claim to have waited 'the full five minutes and more' before cancelling at 07:48:40 is measured from his own tap, not from the geofence entry, and is not the measurement the clause uses. On the clause's clock he had 210 seconds, not 300, and the fee fails.

Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 fails as well as limb (c). No qualifying in-geofence fix falls at or before the 07:41:40 arrived event: the trace's single in-geofence interval begins at 07:45:10, so the record does not place the driver inside the pickup radius when he marked arrival, and the system notice 'Your driver has arrived' sent at 07:41:41 is likewise uncorroborated by any in-radius fix. I do not assert the marker is false under POL-NS-05, because the derived facts fix neither the driver's distance nor his speed at the marker time and I do not compute geometry myself; the point stands without it, because the waiting clock runs from 07:45:10 in any event.

The rider's own track places him at the pickup for the whole wait. All 47 rider fixes qualify, spanning 07:41:40 to 07:48:34, and his greatest distance from the pickup pin across that window is 22.86 m - well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. That corroborates his account that he was waiting at the pickup, and it directly contradicts the driver's assertion that 'Rider did not board': a rider cannot have failed to appear at a pin he was standing within 23 m of throughout. POL-NS-04's separate exoneration route additionally requires a rider chat message, and this log holds only the system arrival notice and the driver's one-word 'here', so I do not rest the fee on that route; the presence measure that clause fixes is what is engaged here.

There is no traffic advisory covering this pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00402-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-NS-06(i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a present and populated advisory of an admissible type covers the pickup road and the waiting period, so the driver cannot reach that limb, cannot excuse the 90-second shortfall by it, and may not assert advisory content against an artifact the bundle does not contain. The trace shows a single in-geofence interval in any case, so there is nothing to sum.

No driver compensation is payable on this record. POL-NS-07 compensates the driver only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-06 displaces it here on a 90-second shortfall and states expressly that no compensation is payable on a shortfall. The outcome is therefore a full refund of the $4.00 cancellation fee to the rider, with no driver payment.

Nothing on this record requires escalation, so the case can and should be decided now. On the only profile fields the no-show clauses permit as grounds: driver no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 120 completed_trips_30d (rate 0.008), far below the POL-NS-07 anti-farming pair of 4 or more and above 0.08, and both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) do not fire; the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0; and every artifact carrying a deciding fact - trip record, GPS trace and fare ledger - is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so POL-NS-09(a) and (e) do not fire either.

The amount to be returned is exactly $4.00 and nothing more. The fare ledger carries a single cancellation-fee line of $4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and that figure reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of $4.00 under the fee_schedule resolution rule; base fare, distance, time, ERP, surge and platform fee are all 0.00 on this cancelled trip. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line only, and under POL-GEN-03 the outcome for a filing rider whose whole contested amount is returned is FULL_REFUND of $4.00.

POL-NS-01 limb (a) is satisfied on the face of the record: the trip record for TRP-00402 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-08-17T07:41:40+08:00 and records the termination of the trip by the driver at 07:48:40. The anchor clause's first condition rests on a recorded event, not on the driver's assertion in his statement.

The driver's presence inside the arrival radius rests on clean, unimpaired telemetry. EV-GPS-00402 has 100% coverage, 92 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, and it yields 22 consecutive qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius between 07:45:10 and 07:48:40 - a continuous stationary hold, not a drive-past, and well beyond the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires before a driver is deemed to have arrived at the pickup point. This is not a driver who never came to the pickup.

The rider's own device track places the rider at the pickup pin throughout the waiting window - 47 qualifying fixes, every sample at 0.0 km/h, between 14.42 m and 22.86 m of the recorded pin (mean 18.76 m) from 07:41:40 to 07:48:34 - while the driver's qualifying fixes sit inside the 50 m radius over the closing 210 seconds. The failed pickup is therefore not a wrong-face-of-the-venue or pin-ambiguity problem that POL-NS-03 would charge to this driver: both parties were a few tens of metres from the same recorded pickup pin, and with trip_record.registered_pickup_points at 1 the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill limb cannot arise in any event.

The record shows no boarding event and a driver-terminated trip under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three codes POL-NS-01 limb (d) recognises; the code is not DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, so there is no driver admission that he could not find the rider and no mis-selected-code finding on that ground. The rider's assertion that the driver 'was not there' is not borne out for the closing 210 seconds of the wait, during which the driver's device is inside the arrival radius on 22 consecutive fixes at 10-second cadence.

The driver does not contend that the full free waiting period is shown on the trace. The longest qualifying in-geofence run measures 210 seconds against the 300 seconds carried by trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec for this trip - a shortfall of 90 seconds - and POL-NS-01(c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 07:41:40 'arrived' event, so the driver cannot and does not start the clock at the button press. That shortfall is an arithmetic shortfall under POL-NS-06. It is not, however, evidence of an absent driver: the same trace shows no gap, no accuracy failure and full coverage, so it records a driver who held the pickup point for three and a half minutes and cancelled from inside the radius, not a driver who never arrived and harvested a fee.

The anti-farming check of POL-NS-07 does not trip on either of the two fields that clause names: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, far below the limb requiring 4 or more, and driver_profile.completed_trips_30d is 120, giving a rate of 0.008 against the limb's 0.08. No withholding of driver compensation and no escalation on that ground is supported on this record, and under POL-GEN-01 no other profile field - including the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter - may be substituted for the two trailing-window fields the clause actually names.

ledger.claim: Nothing on the driver's side of this record shows the repeat-dealing or abuse pattern POL-NS-09 looks for, on the only fields that clause names: driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, so limb (c)'s requirement of two or more no-show disputes between these same parties in 90 days is not met, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so limb (d)'s rider-abuse indicator is absent.

The chat log shows a driver who announced his presence promptly and a rider who said nothing: the only party message in the window is the driver's 'here' at 07:41:50, ten seconds after the platform's 'Your driver has arrived' notice at 07:41:41, with no message from the rider at all. The rider-exonerating route of POL-NS-04 is therefore not made out on limb (a), which requires a locating or coordinating message from the rider; whatever the arithmetic of the dwell, this is not a case of a rider whose message the driver ignored.

The amount charged is the amount the schedule fixes and is internally consistent: the ledger charges exactly the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee in force for this STANDARD, RYDE_X trip - platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.00, agreeing with both the zone-class and vehicle-tier figures - with a waiting-time line of 0.00 and no double charge, so the fare_breakdown reconciles with the fee schedule and no POL-NS-08(d) integrity defect attaches to the figure in dispute.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties.

Outcome: the $4.00 cancellation fee charged on TRP-00402 (EV-FARE-00402: cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable.

What the driver establishes. I accept that his trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 07:41:40 and that he terminated the trip under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, with no DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE admission. I also accept that he really did come to the pickup: EV-GPS-00402 (complete, 92 fixes at 10 s, no gaps, weight 1.0) shows 22 consecutive qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, so the rider's assertion that the driver 'was not there' is not borne out for the closing stretch, and POL-NS-02 is satisfied. POL-NS-03 (wrong entrance or wrong block) does not apply, because the stationary fixes are inside the arrival radius; and POL-NS-04 does not assist the rider, because EV-CHAT-00402 contains only the system arrival notice at 07:41:41 and the driver's own 'here' at 07:41:50 - no rider message - so limb (a) is not made out.

Why the fee still fails. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 300 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-00402), not the 180-second default. POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the arrival tap, and that fix is at 07:45:10; the in-geofence run ends at the cancellation at 07:48:40 - 210 seconds, a shortfall of 90 seconds against the 300 required. POL-NS-06 therefore makes the fee not chargeable and refunds it in full, and says expressly that no driver compensation is payable on a shortfall. The waiting clock cannot be started at 07:41:40: limb (b) likewise finds no qualifying in-geofence fix at or before the arrival event, and no POL-NS-05 recomputation is available because the record does not carry the distance and speed at the marker. The driver's own arithmetic (210 seconds measured, 90 seconds short) is accepted - it is the ground of the refund, not a defence of the fee. POL-NS-07 compensation is not reached, because POL-NS-06 displaces POL-NS-01; the anti-farming check (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 120, rate 0.008) and the POL-NS-09 repeat-dealing indicators (both disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0; rider no_show_disputes_30d 0) do not fire, so nothing escalates and nothing is withheld on those grounds. The ledger reconciles with the schedule (no POL-NS-08(d) defect), and the amount to be returned is exactly the $4.00 cancellation-fee line - base fare, distance, time, ERP, surge and platform fee are all 0.00.

Weight and confidence. The deciding facts - the measured dwell (EV-GPS-00402) and the free waiting period in force (EV-TRIP-00402) - are carried by artifacts at weight 1.0, none impaired under POL-NS-08(a)-(d), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. EV-ADVIS-00402-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and is named here as POL-GEN-02(3) requires: it carries no deciding fact, because POL-NS-06(i) summation is unnecessary on a single in-geofence interval and nothing in this ruling rests on it.

One open question, noted for the record rather than as a referral: the trace places the driver outside the arrival radius from the arrival marker until 07:45:10, so the marker is unsupported, but the record lacks the distance and speed figures POL-NS-05 requires to call it false, and no clause therefore produces a referral on that point.

The monetary effect, $4.00, is at or below the $8.00 execution threshold, so the refund executes automatically on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
